summary.text: Andrew Clyde is the Republican U.S. Representative for Georgia's 9th Congressional District, which he has represented since January 2021, and won re-election on November 3, 2026, according to unofficial results.
A Navy veteran of 28 years, he founded the firearms retailer Clyde Armory in Athens before entering politics.
He serves on the House Appropriations and Budget Committees.

paragraphs.text: Clyde was born November 22, 1963, according to Wikipedia, which lists his birthplace as Walkerton, Ontario, Canada, and says he grew up in Indiana and New York.

He earned his commission from the University of Notre Dame and served as a U.S. Navy officer for 28 years, including three combat deployments to Kuwait and Iraq, according to his official House biography.
After his discharge, he settled in Athens, Georgia, and earned a master's degree in corporate finance and entrepreneurship from the University of Georgia.
He established Clyde Armory in 1991 and, according to his official biography, grew it into a nationwide firearms business that now operates two retail locations in Georgia.

Clyde ran in 2020 for the open 9th District seat after Doug Collins did not seek re-election. He won the August 11 Republican primary runoff over state Rep. Matt Gurtler and defeated Democrat Devin Pandy in the November general election.

He took office January 3, 2021. In the 119th Congress (2025-2026) he sits on the House Appropriations Committee, with seats on its Subcommittees on Commerce-Justice-Science and on Labor-HHS-Education, and on the House Budget Committee.
According to his official biography, Clyde and his wife, Jennifer, live in Jackson County, Georgia.
He won the November 3, 2026 general election with 59.3% of the vote to Caitlyn Gegen's 40.7%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
